- `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`

## Planning ref
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: c589d92f613cfb0cf82aea8a8321070713e27fc1, branch `main`. The integration branch mismatch value is `unknown`, not `true`, so this is not blocked.
- Dependency PR #9515 (commit 8ed137c) is on this ref. All three steps are in job `orchestrate-poll` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - `Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)` at about line 4242, with `if: strategy.job-index == 0`.
  - `Review Semble contract test` at about line 4350, with `if: strategy.job-index == 1`.
  - `Clarify sandbox base image pre-seed tests (#6985)` at about line 4362, with `if: strategy.job-index == 1`.
- `ci.yml` is 290,934 bytes now, well under the 480,000-byte guard.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: one new line in each of the three step bodies
- Put this line directly after the existing `set -euo pipefail`, at the same 10-space indent as the rest of the `run: |` body:
  `trap 'echo "step elapsed: ${SECONDS}s"' EXIT`
- The single quotes delay expansion, so `${SECONDS}` is read when the shell exits, not when the trap is set.
- `${SECONDS}` is not a `${{ }}` expression, so GitHub Actions leaves it alone.
- The trap is the second line of each body, before the first command that can exit. That covers the merge-train step's early exits too (collection failure, "No tests collected").
- Nothing else changes: no step `name:`, `if:`, `timeout-minutes`, matrix, comments, or any other body line.
- Checked locally with `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; trap ... EXIT; ( ... ) & wait; x="$(...)"; false'`:
  - The trap printed exactly once and the shell kept exit code 1, so the step's exit status is unchanged.
  - Bash does not run the parent's EXIT trap in `( ... ) &` subshells or `$(...)` substitutions. The merge-train shard subshells therefore do not print extra elapsed lines.
- Each step runs `run:` with GitHub's default `bash -e {0}` in a fresh shell, so `SECONDS` counts from the start of the step.

### 2. `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`: new class `StepElapsedLine10071ContractTest`
- Add it after `MovedHooks9496StepsContractTest`.
- Add two module constants. A grep found no existing match for `10071`, `ELAPSED` or `StepElapsed`, so the names are unique:
  - `STEP_ELAPSED_TRAP_10071 = "trap 'echo \"step elapsed: ${SECONDS}s\"' EXIT"`
  - `STEP_ELAPSED_10071_STEPS`: a tuple of the three step names, reusing `MERGE_TRAIN_STEP_NAME` for the first.
- Tests, using the existing helper `poll_job_step(name)["run"]`:
  - `test_each_step_prints_its_elapsed_seconds`: each step's `run` contains the trap line exactly once.
  - `test_trap_is_set_before_the_first_command`: the trap is the second line of the body, right after `set -euo pipefail`, and comes before the first `python3` and `exit`.
  - `test_trap_prints_on_failure_and_keeps_the_exit_status`: run `bash -c "set -euo pipefail\n<trap line>\nexit 3"` and check two things:
    - The exit code is 3.
    - stdout matches `^step elapsed: \d+s$` exactly once.
  - `test_trap_prints_on_success`: the same run with `exit 0`.
- The existing `MovedHooks9496StepsContractTest` and `MergeTrainStepContractTest` stay as they are. Neither checks the start of a body:
  - `run_merge_train_judge` cuts the body from `mt_ids=()` to the last `fi`, so a line added at the top is outside its cut.
  - The module, `if:` and ownership checks are unaffected.

### 3. `changelog.d/10071-ci-moved-steps-elapsed-line.md` (new)
- Opens with `<!-- changelog: changed -->`, the same as `changelog.d/9496-ci-hooks-merge-train-semble-preseed-to-poll.md`.
- Has one bullet saying:
  - The three steps now print `step elapsed: <n>s` from an EXIT trap, on success and on failure.
  - This follows up the estimate-only step picks of budget-watch issue #9496 / PR #9515, so the next budget-watch pick can read step durations from the log instead of estimating.
  - No name, guard, timeout or matrix changed, and operators have nothing to do.
- Ends with `Refs #9496.`

## Data structures affected
- None in runtime state. Only the two new test constants.

## API or interface changes
- A new line in the CI log, `step elapsed: <n>s`, in the three steps. It is plain text with no `::` workflow-command prefix, and nothing parses it.
- It is not a contractual log prefix, so no `agents.d` fragment is needed.

## Decisions

### D1 — Put the trap right after `set -euo pipefail`
- Chosen: the second line of each body.
- Alternatives considered: putting the echo at the end of the body (skipped on failure, which the issue rules out); putting the trap first, before `set`.
- Why: it fires on every exit path, including the merge-train step's early `exit 1`, and keeps `set -euo pipefail` as the first line.

### D2 — Use the issue's exact text and test the literal line
- Chosen: `trap 'echo "step elapsed: ${SECONDS}s"' EXIT`, checked as a literal string plus a run of the same line in bash.
- Alternatives considered: `printf`; a shared helper script; a regex-only check.
- Why: it is the smallest change and matches the issue's example. A shared script would add a bootstrap dependency to three one-line steps. Running the line in bash proves it prints on failure without changing the exit status.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, secret, permission or token changes. The trap only prints an integer that bash supplies, with nothing user-controlled in the output.
- No new `${{ }}` interpolation, so there is no new injection surface.
- Abuse case: none. The output cannot form a workflow command because it starts with `step elapsed:`.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- **Merge conflicts:** several open PRs touch `ci.yml`: #9968, #9654, #10075, #10085, #10074, #9981, #9359, #9442 and #9396. #9968 and #9654 also touch `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`. The edits are three one-line insertions and one appended test class, so conflicts should be small. Keep the new class self-contained.
- **Cancellation:** if the runner kills the step on `timeout-minutes` with SIGKILL, no trap runs. That is outside what the issue asks for. A normal failure, or a SIGTERM before the kill, still prints.
- **Existing traps:** none of the three bodies sets a trap today (checked), so nothing is overwritten.
- **Byte-equality checks:** no test compares these step bodies byte-for-byte across workflows. `test_judgment_loop_is_identical_across_workflows` covers the poll shard step only.

## Testing considerations
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py`.
- Run `wc -c .github/workflows/ci.yml` and expect about 291,100 bytes, under 480,000.
- The new class fails on base because the trap line is missing, and passes after the change.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends MovedHooks9496StepsContractTest
Scope-mode justification: The issue lists exactly three steps, one log line each, a test and a changelog fragment. The plan delivers all of that and nothing more: no other steps are given timing lines and no shared helper is added. The complete option, a trap that fires on success and on failure plus a test that actually runs the line in bash, costs only a few more lines than a string check. That follows §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed). The new test class sits beside `MovedHooks9496StepsContractTest` and uses its `poll_job_step` helper.
